title: Homeostasis: keeping the body steady
examples: How does my body keep me warm when it is cold outside?
What happens if I eat too much sugar?
Can you explain the negative feedback loop with an example?

explain.say: Today we are learning about homeostasis in the body. Say homeostasis means keeping things steady.
One important thing the body controls is its temperature. If you get too hot, your body cools you down.

items: Body too hot -> Sweating -> Cools body down
Body too cold -> Shivering -> Warms body up

explain.say: Another thing kept steady is blood sugar levels. When you eat food, your blood sugar goes up. The body then uses insulin to bring it down.
The body also controls the amount of water we have. If you drink too much water, your body tries to get rid of the extra. If you lose water, it tries to keep it.
These adjustments are controlled by negative feedback. This means the body works to reverse any change it senses. It brings things back to normal.
Think about when you are exercising and start to sweat. Sweating cools you down, which brings your temperature back to normal. This is a real-life example.

faq.a: Homeostasis is the process where the body maintains a stable internal environment. It keeps things within a narrow, healthy range.
asks: What does it mean to keep the body steady?
How does the body keep itself balanced?

faq.q: Does every body system have to use negative feedback?
faq.a: Most vital systems, like temperature and blood sugar, use negative feedback. This is how they automatically correct deviations.

faq.q: Why is temperature control so important for survival?
faq.a: If body temperature gets too high or too low, our cells cannot function correctly. This can lead to serious health problems.
asks: What happens if I get too hot?
Why must body temperature stay constant?

faq.q: If I drink too much water, how does my body stop me?
faq.a: The kidneys detect the excess water and increase the rate at which they excrete urine. This removes the extra fluid.

faq.q: What is the role of insulin in blood sugar control?
faq.a: Insulin is a hormone released by the pancreas. It helps move excess glucose from the blood into the cells for energy.

facts: Homeostasis is the maintenance of a stable internal environment.
Body temperature is regulated by sweating when too hot.
Insulin helps lower blood sugar levels after eating.
Kidneys play a key role in balancing water levels.

quiz.say: If body temperature rises too high, the body will most likely:
quiz.why: Sweating releases water, which cools the skin and lowers the core temperature.

wrong.0: Breathing changes are not the primary way to cool down.
wrong.1: While drinking helps, the body's immediate response is physical cooling.
wrong.3: Shivering generates heat, making the temperature rise higher.

quiz.say: When blood sugar is too high, the body releases which substance?
quiz.why: Insulin is specifically released to help cells take up and use excess glucose.

wrong.1: Glucagon raises blood sugar, which is the opposite of what is needed.
wrong.2: Adrenaline is mainly for 'fight or flight' reactions, not routine sugar control.
wrong.3: Water balance is controlled by different mechanisms, not directly by sugar levels.

quiz.say: Which process best describes the body correcting itself?
quiz.why: Negative feedback always works to bring a variable back towards its original set point.

wrong.0: The body must detect the change to know it needs to react.
wrong.1: The response is always related to counteracting the detected deviation.
wrong.3: Amplifying would make the problem worse, not solve it.
